subject: Biotechnology
title: Tumor Profiling
description: A quick, practical guide to Tumor Profiling.

hook.text: Two breast cancers can look identical under a microscope — but their mutations are completely different.

buildup.text: Tumor profiling sequences hundreds of cancer genes — identifying the driver mutations that fuel each tumor.

discovery.text: Matched therapies target specific mutations — BRAF inhibitors for melanoma, HER2 antibodies for breast cancer.

twist.text: Tumors are heterogeneous — different cells in the same tumor carry different mutations, complicating treatment.

climax.text: Foundation Medicine's FoundationOne CDx tests 324 genes from a single biopsy — comprehensive profiling in clinical practice.

punchline.text: Sequence the tumor, match the drug — cancer genomics makes treatment personal.

quiz.question: Why is tumor heterogeneity a challenge for targeted therapy?
options: Heterogeneous tumors grow more slowly than uniform ones
Different cells in the same tumor carry different mutations, so one targeted drug may not kill all cells

faq.question: What is an actionable mutation in cancer?
faq.answer: An actionable mutation is one with an approved drug targeting it or one that qualifies the patient for a clinical trial. Examples include EGFR mutations in lung cancer treated with osimertinib and BRAF V600E in melanoma treated with targeted inhibitors.

faq.question: Should all cancer patients get tumor profiling?
faq.answer: NCCN guidelines recommend comprehensive genomic profiling for advanced solid tumors and many hematologic cancers. For early-stage cancers, standard-of-care testing for known biomarkers may suffice. Cost effectiveness improves as more targeted therapies become available and testing costs decrease.
